title: Practice questions (original, not an official bank)
source: Written for this project with an AI assistant; answers checked by calculation or against standard textbook facts. Not taken from any official question bank and not reviewed by an examiner.

questions.question: A 220 Ω resistor is connected across an 11 V battery. What current flows through it?
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: A transmitter draws 2 A from a 13.8 V supply. How much power does it take from the supply?
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Two resistors of 100 Ω and 150 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 100 Ω + 150 Ω = 250 Ω. (60 Ω would be the value for the same two resistors in parallel.)
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Two 100 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel the total is half of one of them: 100 Ω / 2 = 50 Ω.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: In the circuit shown, a 12 V supply is connected across R_{1} = 3 kΩ in series with R_{2} = 1 kΩ. What is the voltage across R_{2}?
questions.explanation: The same current flows through both resistors: I = 12 V / 4 kΩ = 3 mA. The voltage across R_{2} is 3 mA × 1 kΩ = 3 V.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: A cable attenuates a signal by 10 dB. What fraction of the power entering the cable reaches the other end?
questions.explanation: −10 dB is a power ratio of 10^{-1} = 0.1, that is 10 %.

questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which component stores energy in a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: A coil stores energy in its magnetic field; a capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: A fixed resistor is connected to a battery. Which change would double the current through the resistor?
answers: Doubling both the voltage and the resistance
questions.explanation: I = V / R: doubling V doubles I, doubling R halves it, and doubling both leaves I unchanged.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the wavelength of a 14.2 MHz signal, approximately?
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: About what wavelength does a 145 MHz signal have?
questions.explanation: λ = c / f ≈ 300 / 145 MHz ≈ 2.07 m, which is why 144–146 MHz is called the 2 m band.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which ionospheric layer is the most important for long-distance (multi-hop) HF communication?
questions.explanation: The F2 layer is the highest and most strongly ionised region; it refracts HF signals back to earth over the longest distances.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does the D layer mainly do to HF signals during the day?
answers: It absorbs them, mostly on the lowest HF bands
It reflects them over long distances
It has no effect on HF signals
questions.explanation: The D layer exists only in daylight and absorbs low-frequency HF signals (for example 160 m and 80 m), which is why those bands work best at night.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: If the frequency of a radio wave is doubled, what happens to its wavelength?
questions.explanation: λ = c / f: the wavelength is inversely proportional to the frequency.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which kind of propagation is normally used for local VHF and UHF contacts?
answers: Ground wave along the surface over hundreds of kilometres
questions.explanation: VHF and UHF waves are not normally refracted back by the ionosphere; ordinary contacts rely on the direct path, slightly extended beyond the horizon.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the “skip zone”?
answers: The part of the ionosphere that absorbs signals
The area too far for the ground wave and too close for the sky wave to arrive
The area right below the antenna where the signal is strongest
The time of day when a band is closed
questions.explanation: The ground wave dies out after a limited distance, and the sky wave comes back to earth only beyond a minimum distance: in between lies the skip zone.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Roughly how long is a half-wave wire dipole for 7.1 MHz, allowing for the usual end-effect shortening of about 5 %?
questions.explanation: The free-space half wavelength is 300 / 7.1 / 2 ≈ 21.1 m; shortening it by about 5 % gives ≈ 20 m (the common rule L ≈ 143 / f in MHz gives 20.1 m).
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the approximate feed-point impedance of a half-wave dipole in free space?
questions.explanation: A thin half-wave dipole in free space has a feed-point resistance of about 73 Ω; a folded dipole has about 300 Ω.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: The forward power is 100 W and the reflected power is 4 W. What is the SWR?
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: An antenna has a gain of 3 dBd. What is that gain in dBi?
questions.explanation: The gain of a half-wave dipole over an isotropic radiator is 2.15 dB, so dBi = dBd + 2.15.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: A transmitter delivers 10 W through a lossless feed line to an antenna with 3 dBd gain. What is the ERP (relative to a dipole)?
questions.explanation: +3 dB is a factor of about 2 in power: 10 W × 2 ≈ 20 W.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does a balun do?
answers: It increases the transmitter output power
It connects a balanced antenna to an unbalanced feed line, or the reverse
questions.explanation: A balun (balanced–unbalanced transformer) matches a balanced antenna such as a dipole to an unbalanced coaxial cable.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which characteristic impedance is the most common for coaxial cable in amateur stations?
questions.explanation: Most amateur transmitters and antennas are designed for 50 Ω; 75 Ω coax is mainly used for television and cable systems.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: The wire antenna in the figure is fed in the middle, and each half is a quarter of a wavelength long. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Two quarter-wave arms fed at the centre make a half-wave dipole.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which of these antennas has the greatest gain in one direction?
questions.explanation: Adding a reflector and directors concentrates the radiation in one direction; the other choices have less gain, and an isotropic radiator is the 0 dBi reference.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which of these ways of sending speech needs the narrowest bandwidth?
questions.explanation: An SSB voice signal occupies about 2.4 kHz, an AM signal about 6 kHz, narrow-band FM roughly 10–15 kHz and broadcast FM about 180 kHz.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the purpose of a low-pass filter at the output of an HF transmitter?
answers: To attenuate harmonics and other emissions above the operating frequency
questions.explanation: The filter lets the wanted frequency through and weakens harmonics, which could otherwise interfere with other services.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the selectivity of a receiver?
answers: Its ability to separate the wanted signal from signals on nearby frequencies
Its ability to hear very weak signals
Its speed of tuning across a band
questions.explanation: Selectivity is about rejecting neighbours; the ability to receive weak signals is called sensitivity.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the second harmonic of a 7.1 MHz transmission?
questions.explanation: The n-th harmonic is n × f: 2 × 7.1 MHz = 14.2 MHz (the third would be 21.3 MHz).
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: In a superheterodyne receiver, which stage converts the incoming signal to the intermediate frequency?
questions.explanation: The mixer combines the signal with the local oscillator; the difference frequency is the intermediate frequency (IF).
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the main job of automatic gain control (AGC) in a receiver?
answers: To keep the output level nearly constant as the signal strength changes
questions.explanation: AGC reduces the gain for strong signals and raises it for weak ones, so the loudness stays steady.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: How is a CW (Morse code) signal produced?
answers: By varying the carrier frequency with speech
By switching (keying) a carrier on and off
By suppressing the carrier and sending one sideband
By changing the polarisation of the carrier
questions.explanation: CW is on–off keying of an unmodulated carrier in the pattern of the Morse code.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which word stands for the letter K in the international spelling alphabet?
questions.explanation: ICAO/NATO spelling alphabet: … Juliet, Kilo, Lima …
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does the Q-code QTH refer to?
questions.explanation: QTH = location. (QRG = frequency, QRM = interference from other stations, QRP = low power.)
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does the Q-code QRM mean?
questions.explanation: QRM = man-made interference; QRN = natural noise; QRP = reduce power; QSY = change frequency.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does the Q-code QSY mean?
questions.explanation: QSY = “change to another frequency”.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does an RS report of 59 tell the other station?
questions.explanation: R5 means perfectly readable and S9 a very strong signal (“five nine”).
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the meaning of the call “CQ”?
answers: I am about to close down
A general call to any station that hears it
questions.explanation: CQ invites any station to reply; “CQ CQ CQ de” followed by the call sign is the usual form.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What does “73” mean in amateur radio?
questions.explanation: 73 = best regards (88 = love and kisses).
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: In Morse operating, which prosign normally means “end of contact”?
questions.explanation: SK ends a contact; K = go ahead, BK = break, R = received.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the first thing to do before opening a mains-powered power supply for repair?
answers: Switch it on to find the fault
Touch the case to check for voltage
Disconnect it from the mains and let the capacitors discharge
questions.explanation: Mains voltage can be lethal, and large capacitors can stay charged after switching off.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the most serious danger of putting a wire antenna near overhead power lines?
answers: The antenna would radiate less power
If it falls or touches a line, it can carry a lethal voltage
The mains would be interrupted every time you transmit
questions.explanation: A falling antenna or a contact with a line puts mains voltage on the wire and on the person touching it.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: What is the safest course when a thunderstorm approaches and you have an outdoor antenna?
answers: Transmit with extra power to discharge it
Disconnect the antenna from the equipment and stay away from it
Touch the coax shield to check for static
Stand next to the mast to protect it
questions.explanation: Lightning can travel down the feed line; disconnected cables and distance reduce the risk to people and equipment.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: If you double your distance from a transmitting antenna (in the far field), what happens to the power density?
questions.explanation: Power density follows the inverse-square law: 1 / 2^{2} = 1/4.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: A transmitter’s harmonics disturb television reception. Which filter fitted at the transmitter output helps?
questions.explanation: The harmonics lie above the operating frequency, so a low-pass filter weakens them.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)

questions.question: Which measure keeps a metal equipment case from staying live if an internal mains wire touches it?
answers: A plastic knob on the case
A protective earth connection together with a fuse or residual-current device
questions.explanation: The earth connection lets a fault current flow, and the fuse or RCD then cuts the supply.
questions.source: Original question written for this project (not from an official bank)
